q: World Hindi Day, observed on 10th January every year, commemorates:

options.A: The holding of the First World Hindi Conference at Nagpur in January 1975
options.B: The adoption of Hindi as the Official Language by the Constituent Assembly
options.C: The enactment of the Official Languages Act, 1963
options.D: The appointment of the first Official Language Commission

e: World Hindi Day, observed on 10th January every year, commemorates the holding of the First World Hindi Conference at Nagpur in January 1975.

q: The Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar and the Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar of the Department of Official Language are presented every year on the occasion of:
e: The Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar and the Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar of the Department of Official Language are presented every year on Hindi Diwas (14th September), the main annual occasion for the Official Language.

q: Under the three-language formula, the three languages to be studied in the non-Hindi speaking States are:

options.B: The regional language, Hindi and English
options.C: The regional language, English and Urdu
options.D: Hindi, the regional language and French

e: Under the three-language formula, the three languages studied in the non-Hindi speaking States are the regional language, Hindi and English.

q: Hindi Diwas was celebrated for the first time in the year:
e: Hindi Diwas marks the adoption of Hindi as the official language on 14th September 1949, and it was celebrated for the first time in the year 1953.

q: The Official Language Commission under Article 344 of the Constitution is appointed by:
e: Under Article 344, the Official Language Commission is appointed by the President at the expiration of five years, and thereafter at the expiration of ten years, from the commencement of the Constitution.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 350A, the duty to provide facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage rests on the Central Government alone.
2. Under Article 350A, the President may issue such directions to any State as he considers necessary or proper for securing the provision of such facilities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is wrong: Article 350A places the endeavour on every State and every local authority, not on the Central Government alone. Statement 2 is correct: the President may issue directions to a State to secure such facilities.

q: Under the Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi, the target fixed for issuing the documents specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 in both Hindi and English is:
e: The documents specified in Section 3(3) must invariably be issued in both Hindi and English, so the Annual Programme fixes a target of 100 per cent for them.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "No Objection Certificate" is:
e: "Anapatti Praman Patra" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "No Objection Certificate" in the official glossary of administrative terms.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Fixation of Pay" is:
e: "Vetan Niyatan" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Fixation of Pay", the determination of pay on appointment, promotion or revision of scales.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Agenda" (of a meeting) is:
e: "Karyasuchi" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Agenda", the list of items of business placed before a meeting.

q: Chapter I of Part XVII of the Constitution (Articles 343 and 344) is titled:

options.C: Language of the Supreme Court and the High Courts

e: Chapter I of Part XVII (Articles 343 and 344) deals with the official language of the Union and is titled "Language of the Union".

q: Chapter III of Part XVII of the Constitution (Articles 348 and 349) is titled:

options.B: Language of the Supreme Court, the High Courts, etc.

e: Chapter III of Part XVII (Articles 348 and 349) deals with the language of the Supreme Court, the High Courts and the authoritative texts of Bills and Acts, as its title shows.

q: Part XVII of the Constitution, which deals with the Official Language, comprises Articles 343 to 351, i.e., a total of:
e: Part XVII comprises Articles 343 to 351, that is, a total of nine articles dealing with the Official Language.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 345, a State Legislature may adopt Hindi as one of the official languages of the State even if Hindi is not in use in that State.
2. The language or languages adopted by a State Legislature under Article 345 become the official language or languages of that State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: Article 345 empowers a State Legislature to adopt any language in use in the State, or Hindi, as an official language even if Hindi is not in use there, and the language so adopted becomes the official language of that State.

q: Under Article 347 of the Constitution, where the President directs that a language spoken by a substantial proportion of the population of a State shall be officially recognised, such recognition may be:

options.A: For the whole or any part of the State and for such purposes as he may specify
options.C: Only for use in the courts of that State
options.D: Only for a period of five years at a time

e: Under Article 347, when the President is satisfied that a substantial proportion of a State's population desires it, he may direct official recognition of their language for the whole or any part of the State and for the purposes he specifies.

q: Under Article 350A of the Constitution, it shall be the endeavour of ______ to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage of education to children belonging to linguistic minority groups.

options.C: The District Magistrate of the district
options.D: Every State and every local authority within the State

e: Article 350A provides that it shall be the endeavour of every State and every local authority within the State to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage to children of linguistic minority groups.

q: Under Article 350B of the Constitution, it shall be the duty of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities:

options.A: To promote the use of Hindi in the minority areas
options.B: To investigate all matters relating to the safeguards provided for linguistic minorities under the Constitution
options.C: To conduct the decennial census in minority areas
options.D: To inspect Hindi training centres in the States

e: Under Article 350B, it is the duty of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities to investigate all matters relating to the safeguards provided for linguistic minorities under the Constitution.

q: Under Article 351 of the Constitution, Hindi shall be enriched, without interfering with its genius, by assimilating the forms, style and expressions used in:

options.C: Hindustani and the other languages of India specified in the Eighth Schedule

e: Article 351 directs that Hindi shall be enriched by assimilating, without interfering with its genius, the forms, style and expressions used in Hindustani and in the other languages of India specified in the Eighth Schedule.

q: Under Article 210 of the Constitution, a member of the Legislature of a State who is unable to express himself adequately in the official language of the State, in Hindi or in English, may address the House in:

options.A: His mother tongue, with the permission of the presiding officer
options.C: Any language included in the Eighth Schedule of another State

e: Under Article 210, a member of a State Legislature who is unable to express himself adequately in the official language of the State, in Hindi or in English, may address the House in his mother tongue with the permission of the presiding officer.

q: Which of the following is required to be issued in both Hindi and English under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963?

options.A: A confidential note recorded on a file
options.B: A representation submitted by an employee
options.C: A personal letter written by an officer
options.D: Rules, regulations and bye-laws issued by a Central Government office

e: Rules, regulations and bye-laws are among the documents specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 and must be issued in both Hindi and English; file notes, representations and personal letters are not in that list.

q: Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, an agreement entered into by a Central Government office is required to be executed in:

options.D: The regional language of the State only

e: Agreements are among the documents specified in Section 3(3), so an agreement entered into by a Central Government office is required to be executed in both Hindi and English.

q: The Chairman of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is:

options.B: The Union Home Minister, ex officio
options.C: Elected by the members of the Committee from amongst themselves
options.D: The senior-most member of the Rajya Sabha on the Committee

e: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language elects its Chairman from amongst its own members.

q: The Department of Official Language is a department of the:
e: The Department of Official Language is a department of the Ministry of Home Affairs and is the nodal department for implementing the Official Language Policy of the Union.

q: The Vice-Chairman of the Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee) is the:
e: The Union Home Minister is the Vice-Chairman of the Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee), which is chaired by the Prime Minister.

q: The Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti is chaired by the:

options.C: General Manager of the senior-most Zonal Railway

e: The Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti, which advises the Ministry of Railways on Official Language matters, is chaired by the Minister of Railways.

q: In-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is compulsory for those Central Government employees who:

options.A: Have passed the matriculation examination with Hindi as a subject
options.B: Have already passed the Pragya examination
options.C: Do not possess working knowledge of Hindi
options.D: Have attained the age of 45 years

e: In-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is compulsory for those Central Government employees who do not possess working knowledge of Hindi; the others do not need it.

q: Under the incentive scheme for doing original noting and drafting in Hindi, an employee becomes eligible for consideration for a cash award on doing noting and drafting in Hindi of at least:
e: Under the incentive scheme for doing original noting and drafting in Hindi, an employee becomes eligible for consideration for a cash award on doing at least 10,000 words of noting and drafting in Hindi in a year.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of Uttar Pradesh is placed in:

options.D: It is not placed in any region

e: Uttar Pradesh is a Hindi-speaking State where Hindi is the official language and is widely understood, so it is placed in Region 'A'.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of Himachal Pradesh is placed in:

options.C: It is not placed in any region

e: Himachal Pradesh is a Hindi-speaking State and is accordingly placed in Region 'A' under the Official Language Rules.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of Uttarakhand is placed in:

options.D: It is not placed in any region

e: Uttarakhand, where Hindi is the official language and is widely spoken and understood, is placed in Region 'A'.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of Odisha is placed in:

options.D: It is not placed in any region

e: Odisha is a non-Hindi speaking State whose official language is Odia, so it is placed in Region 'C'.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of Andhra Pradesh is placed in:

options.D: It is not placed in any region

e: Andhra Pradesh is a non-Hindi speaking State with Telugu as its official language, and is placed in Region 'C'.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of Goa is placed in:

options.D: It is not placed in any region

e: Goa, where Konkani is the official language, is a non-Hindi speaking State and is placed in Region 'C'.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Jharkhand is placed in Region 'A' under the Official Language Rules.
2. Telangana is placed in Region 'C' under the Official Language Rules.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: Jharkhand, a Hindi-speaking State, is placed in Region 'A', and Telangana, a non-Hindi speaking State, is placed in Region 'C'.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Order" is:
e: "Aadesh" is the standard Hindi equivalent of the administrative term "Order".

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Office Memorandum" is:
e: "Karyalaya Gyapan" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Office Memorandum", the usual form of internal communication in Government offices.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Resolution" is:
e: "Sankalp" is the standard Hindi equivalent of the administrative term "Resolution".

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Gazette" is:
e: "Rajpatra" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Gazette", the official publication in which Government notifications and orders are published.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Corrigendum" is:
e: "Shuddhi Patra" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Corrigendum", issued to correct an error in a document already published.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Minutes" (of a meeting) is:
e: "Karyavritt" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Minutes", the formal record of the proceedings and decisions of a meeting.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Tender" is:
e: "Nivida" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Tender", the invitation of bids or offers for a work or supply.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Suspension" is:
e: "Nilamban" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Suspension", the temporary removal of an employee from duty pending proceedings.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Earned Leave" is:
e: "Arjit Avakash" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Earned Leave", the leave earned by duty performed.

q: The Official Language Implementation Committee of the headquarters office of a Zonal Railway is chaired by the:
e: The Official Language Implementation Committee of the headquarters office of a Zonal Railway is chaired by the General Manager, who heads the Zonal Railway.

q: In a Railway Division, the day-to-day work relating to the implementation of the Official Language Policy is looked after by the:
e: In a Railway Division, the day-to-day work of implementing the Official Language Policy is looked after by the Rajbhasha Adhikari (Official Language Officer) of the Division.

q: Which of the following statements about the language position under the Constitution of India is correct?

options.A: Hindi is declared the national language of India
options.B: English is declared the national language of India
options.C: Sanskrit is declared the national language of India
options.D: The Constitution does not declare any language as the national language; Hindi in Devanagari script is the official language of the Union

e: The Constitution declares no language as the national language of India; under Article 343, Hindi in Devanagari script is the official language of the Union.

q: After the amendment of the Official Languages Act in 1967, English continues to be used for the official purposes of the Union as:

options.A: An associate official language, in addition to Hindi
options.B: The sole official language of the Union
options.C: A language confined to court work only
options.D: A foreign language for external affairs only

e: After the amendment of the Official Languages Act in 1967, English continues to be used, in addition to Hindi, as an associate official language for the official purposes of the Union.

q: The compromise formula on the official language question, adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 14th September, 1949, is known as the:
e: The compromise formula on the official language question adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 14th September 1949 is known as the Munshi-Ayyangar formula.

q: The authoritative text of the Constitution of India in the Hindi language is published under the authority of the President in accordance with:
e: The authoritative text of the Constitution in Hindi is published under the authority of the President in accordance with Article 394A.

q: The Parangat course, meant for employees who have passed Pragya and require advanced proficiency in Hindi, is conducted through correspondence by the:

options.C: Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology

e: The Parangat course, an advanced course meant for employees who have passed Pragya, is conducted through correspondence by the Central Hindi Directorate.

q: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications from a Central Government office to an office of a State Government located in Region 'A' shall be in:

options.C: The regional language of the State

e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications from a Central Government office to an office of a State Government located in Region 'A' shall ordinarily be in Hindi.

q: The Quarterly Progress Report on the progressive use of Hindi is submitted by a Central Government office to:

options.A: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language, directly
options.C: Its controlling office / administrative Ministry or Department

e: The Quarterly Progress Report on the progressive use of Hindi is submitted by a Central Government office to its controlling office or administrative Ministry or Department, which monitors the implementation.

q: The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities functions under the:
e: The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities functions under the Ministry of Minority Affairs, which deals with the safeguards for minorities, including linguistic minorities.

q: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language functioning at present is constituted under:

options.C: Rule 12 of the Official Language Rules, 1976
options.D: Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963

e: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language functioning at present is constituted under Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963.

q: The recommendations of the first Official Language Commission (Kher Commission) were examined by a Committee of Parliament whose Chairman was:
e: The recommendations of the first Official Language Commission (Kher Commission) were examined by a Committee of Parliament whose Chairman was G. B. Pant.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. During the first fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution, the President could, by order, authorise the use of the Hindi language in addition to the English language for any of the official purposes of the Union.
2. During the same period, the President could also authorise the use of the Devanagari form of numerals in addition to the international form of Indian numerals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: under Article 343, during the first fifteen years the President could by order authorise the use of Hindi in addition to English, and the Devanagari form of numerals in addition to the international form, for official purposes of the Union.

q: Under Article 210(2) of the Constitution, the use of the English language for transacting business in the Legislature of a State was to cease on the expiration of fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution, unless:

options.B: The Legislature of the State by law otherwise provides
options.C: The Governor of the State directs otherwise
options.D: The President by order otherwise provides

e: Under Article 210(2), the use of English for transacting business in a State Legislature was to cease after fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution, unless the Legislature of the State by law otherwise provides.

q: The "international form of Indian numerals" referred to in Article 343 of the Constitution means:

options.A: The numerals 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 0, as used internationally
options.C: The Roman numerals I, II, III, IV and so on
options.D: The numerals of the respective regional scripts

e: The "international form of Indian numerals" in Article 343 means the numerals 1, 2, 3 and so on up to 0, the ordinary Arabic figures in international use, as distinct from Devanagari numerals.

q: The use of Hindi in the proceedings of the High Court has been authorised by the Governor with the previous consent of the President in the States of:

options.B: West Bengal, Odisha, Assam and Kerala
options.C: Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
options.D: Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan

e: The use of Hindi in the proceedings of the High Court has been authorised by the Governor, with the previous consent of the President, in Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan.

q: How many Official Language Commissions have been constituted under Article 344 of the Constitution so far?
e: Only one Official Language Commission, the Kher Commission appointed in 1955, has been constituted under Article 344 of the Constitution so far.

q: Article 394A of the Constitution, which provides for the authoritative text of the Constitution in the Hindi language, was inserted by:
e: Article 394A, which provides for the authoritative text of the Constitution in the Hindi language, was inserted by the Constitution (58th Amendment) Act, 1987.

q: The Marathi language, included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, is officially written in the:
e: Marathi, a language included in the Eighth Schedule, is officially written in the Devanagari script.

q: The Santhali language, included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, is written in the:
e: Santhali, included in the Eighth Schedule, is written in the Ol Chiki script, which was devised specially for the language.

q: The Manipuri language included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution is also known as:
e: The Manipuri language included in the Eighth Schedule is also known as Meitei (Meiteilon), the language of the Meitei people of Manipur.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. English is the official language of the State of Nagaland.
2. English is the official language of the State of Arunachal Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: English is the official language of Nagaland as well as of Arunachal Pradesh, both non-Hindi speaking States of the North-East.

q: The official language of the State of Goa is:
e: Konkani is the official language of the State of Goa.

q: The Maithili language is mainly spoken in the Mithila region of the State of:
e: Maithili is mainly spoken in the Mithila region of Bihar, where it has a long literary tradition.

q: The Dogri language is mainly spoken in which region?
e: Dogri is mainly spoken in the Jammu region.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Chhattisgarh is placed in Region 'A' under the Official Language Rules.
2. Puducherry is placed in Region 'C' under the Official Language Rules.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: Chhattisgarh, a Hindi-speaking State, is placed in Region 'A', and the Union Territory of Puducherry is placed in Region 'C'.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the Union Territory of Lakshadweep is placed in:

options.D: It is not placed in any region

e: Lakshadweep, a non-Hindi speaking Union Territory where Malayalam is mainly used, is placed in Region 'C' under the Official Language Rules.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of Sikkim is placed in:

options.C: It is not placed in any region

e: Sikkim is a non-Hindi speaking State and is placed in Region 'C' under the Official Language Rules.

q: Under Article 350B of the Constitution, the reports of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities are caused to be laid before each House of Parliament, and sent to the Governments of the States concerned, by:

options.A: The Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities himself

e: Under Article 350B, the reports of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities are laid before each House of Parliament and sent to the Governments of the States concerned by the President.

q: The Central Translation Bureau (Kendriya Anuvad Bureau) was set up in the year:
e: The Central Translation Bureau (Kendriya Anuvad Bureau), which handles translation of codes, manuals and other non-statutory material of Central Government offices, was set up in the year 1971.

q: Besides the translation of codes, manuals and other non-statutory material, the Central Translation Bureau also conducts:

options.A: Translation training programmes for the translators of Central Government offices
options.B: The Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations
options.C: Inspection of Central Government offices for use of Hindi
options.D: Hindi typewriting classes for clerical staff

e: Besides translation of codes, manuals and other non-statutory material, the Central Translation Bureau also conducts translation training programmes for the translators of Central Government offices.

q: The Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (Central Institute of Hindi) at Agra is mainly engaged in:

options.A: Translating Central Acts and Ordinances into Hindi
options.B: Conducting the examinations of the Hindi Teaching Scheme
options.C: Inspecting railway offices for implementation of the Official Language Policy
options.D: Teaching Hindi to non-Hindi speaking Indian and foreign learners, training of Hindi teachers and research in Hindi

e: The Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (Central Institute of Hindi) at Agra is mainly engaged in teaching Hindi to non-Hindi speaking Indian and foreign learners, training Hindi teachers and carrying on research in Hindi.

q: The Regional Implementation Offices of the Department of Official Language, set up in different parts of the country, are mainly responsible for:

options.A: Translating the codes and manuals of Central Government offices
options.B: Conducting Hindi examinations of Central Government employees
options.C: Monitoring and inspecting the implementation of the Official Language Policy in the Central Government offices located in their respective regions
options.D: Printing bilingual forms and stationery for all Central Government offices

e: The Regional Implementation Offices of the Department of Official Language are responsible for monitoring and inspecting the implementation of the Official Language Policy in the Central Government offices located in their respective regions.

q: World Hindi Day, observed on 10th January every year, was observed for the first time in the year:
e: World Hindi Day, observed on 10th January every year, was observed for the first time in the year 2006.

q: The Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi, containing the targets to be achieved by Central Government offices, is issued by the Department of Official Language:

options.D: Only when the Committee of Parliament on Official Language so recommends

e: The Annual Programme containing the targets for the progressive use of Hindi to be achieved by Central Government offices is issued by the Department of Official Language every year.

q: The three-language formula for school education was first recommended by:
e: The three-language formula for school education was first recommended by the Education Commission (Kothari Commission), 1964-66.

q: The First World Hindi Conference, held at Nagpur in January 1975, was inaugurated by:

options.C: Smt. Indira Gandhi, the then Prime Minister

e: The First World Hindi Conference, held at Nagpur in January 1975, was inaugurated by Smt. Indira Gandhi, the then Prime Minister of India.

q: Where the use of Hindi for judgments, decrees or orders of a High Court has been authorised under Section 7 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, every such judgment, decree or order shall be accompanied by:

options.A: A translation thereof in the English language issued under the authority of the High Court
options.B: A summary of the judgment in the regional language
options.C: A certificate of the Registrar of the High Court
options.D: A Hindi translation of the English text

e: Under Section 7 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, where Hindi is used for a High Court judgment, decree or order, it shall be accompanied by a translation thereof in English issued under the authority of the High Court.

q: To ensure that the documents specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 are invariably issued in both Hindi and English, Central Government offices designate certain points in the office, such as the despatch section, which are known as:
e: To ensure that Section 3(3) documents are invariably issued in both Hindi and English, offices designate certain points, such as the despatch section, as "Check Points" where bilingual issue is verified.

q: The Bodo language, included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, is written in the:
e: The Bodo language, included in the Eighth Schedule by the 92nd Amendment, is written in the Devanagari script.

q: In the State of Goa, Konkani, the official language of the State, is used in the:
e: In Goa, Konkani, the official language of the State, is officially used in the Devanagari script.

q: Sanskrit has been declared as the second official language of the State of:
e: Sanskrit has been declared as the second official language of the State of Uttarakhand.

q: The World Hindi Secretariat (Vishwa Hindi Sachivalaya) has its headquarters in:
e: The World Hindi Secretariat (Vishwa Hindi Sachivalaya), set up to promote Hindi at the international level, has its headquarters in Mauritius.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Promotion" is:
e: "Padonnati" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Promotion", the advancement of an employee to a higher post or grade.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Retirement" is:
e: "Sevanivritti" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Retirement", the cessation of service on attaining the prescribed age or otherwise.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Allowance" is:
e: "Bhatta" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Allowance", a payment made in addition to pay for a specific purpose.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Annexure" is:
e: "Anulagnak" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Annexure", a document attached to and forming part of a main document.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Appointment" is:
e: "Niyukti" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Appointment", the engagement of a person to a post.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Dismissal" is:
e: "Barkhastagi" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Dismissal", the removal of an employee from service as a penalty.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Verification" is:
e: "Satyapan" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Verification", the checking of a fact, record or document for correctness.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Enclosure" is:
e: "Sanlagnak" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Enclosure", a paper enclosed with a letter or document.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Confidential" is:
e: "Gopaniya" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Confidential", denoting matter that is not to be disclosed.

q: On the occasion of Hindi Diwas, the employees of Central Government offices take:

options.B: A pledge to pass the Hindi typing examination
options.C: The Rajbhasha pledge (Rajbhasha Pratigya), to use Hindi to the maximum possible extent in their official work

e: On the occasion of Hindi Diwas, employees of Central Government offices take the Rajbhasha pledge (Rajbhasha Pratigya), resolving to use Hindi to the maximum possible extent in their official work.

q: Which of the following States is NOT placed in Region 'A' under the Official Language Rules?
e: Punjab is placed in Region 'B', not Region 'A'; Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jharkhand are Hindi-speaking States placed in Region 'A'.

q: Which of the following is NOT placed in Region 'C' under the Official Language Rules?
e: Gujarat is placed in Region 'B', not Region 'C'; Kerala, Assam and Sikkim are all placed in Region 'C'.

q: After the inclusion of Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali in the Eighth Schedule in the year 1992, the total number of languages included in the Eighth Schedule became:
e: Before 1992 the Eighth Schedule had 15 languages; the addition of Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali in that year raised the total to 18.

q: The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution does NOT include which one of the following languages?
e: Tulu is not included in the Eighth Schedule, whereas Santhali, Dogri and Maithili were all added to it by the Constitution (92nd Amendment) Act, 2003.
